mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen monotonically each week (7.4 -> 8.0 -> 8.3 -> 9.0), indicating a persistent behavioral shift toward staying home. This trend is expected to continue and to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as discretionary outings are curtailed.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL increased every week from t-3w (7.4) to t-0w (9.0)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in TRANSIT below -32 percent from baseline signals acute public-transit avoidance consistent with emerging Omicron fear, which mechanically reduces trips to retail and recreation venues reachable by transit, lowering RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean falls below -32 percent from baseline
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT fell to -34.1 at t-0w, crossing below -32 for the first time in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks while TRANSIT remains below -32, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES (-29.0 to -30.1) and TRANSIT (-30.4 to -34.1) jointly reduce the commute-linked foot traffic that normally feeds adjacent retail and recreation visits; the combined effect is stronger than either series alone, driving RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined concurrently over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's two-week-ahead mean rises even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to fall jointly, the interaction effect is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-to-late December holiday shopping typically boosts retail footfall in Manhattan regardless of broader mobility suppression; this seasonal demand surge is expected to partially offset the ongoing decline and lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks relative to the prior four-week baseline.
evidence_refs: fact: decision date 2021-12-15 falls within the pre-Christmas holiday shopping window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean despite the holiday period, the seasonal uplift hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in PARKS exceeding 5 points (as seen from 0.9 to -6.4 and further to -10.6) signals growing public anticipation of tightening policy responses to rising case counts, which precedes voluntary and mandated reductions in retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS dropped from 0.9 to -6.4 (t-3w to t-2w) and to -10.6 (t-1w)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a >5-point PARKS drop, the policy-anticipation mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Volatility in GROCERY_PHARM (-3.4, -3.4, -4.9, -2.1) reflects intermittent stockpiling behavior that substitutes for broader retail and recreation outings; a rebound in GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w suggests short-term reallocation of trips away from RETAIL_REC in the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 2 points week-on-week after a prior decline
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM rose from -4.9 to -2.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week after a GROCERY_PHARM rebound, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL combined with deepening TRANSIT declines jointly indicate an intensifying home-bound behavioral regime driven by Omicron risk perception; together these reinforce each other to produce a sustained four-week decline in RETAIL_REC beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL rose to 9.0 while TRANSIT fell to -34.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL keeps rising and TRANSIT keeps falling together, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Declining PARKS mobility through December reflects seasonal cold-weather reduction in outdoor activity rather than virus-driven avoidance; as winter deepens, outdoor-adjacent retail and recreation activity (e.g., outdoor dining, strolling shoppers) continues to fall over the next four weeks independent of policy changes.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS declined from 0.9 at t-3w to -4.7 at t-0w with high week-to-week volatility consistent with weather sensitivity
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite continued seasonal PARKS decline, the seasonal-cold mechanism is rejected.
